issues.title: 26.3 build declares a controlify entrypoint whose class isn't in the jar — crashes on startup with Controlify installed
issues.body:
### Description

Zoomify 2.16.2+26.3 crashes the game during startup whenever Controlify is also
installed. 26.1 and 26.2 are unaffected.

The published jar declares a `controlify` entrypoint pointing at a class the jar does
not contain:

    $ unzip -l zoomify-2.16.2+26.3.jar | grep integrations
       dev/isxander/zoomify/integrations/
       dev/isxander/zoomify/integrations/ModMenuIntegration.class

    $ unzip -p zoomify-2.16.2+26.3.jar fabric.mod.json
       "controlify": [
         { "adapter": "kotlin",
           "value": "dev.isxander.zoomify.integrations.ControlifyIntegration" }
       ]

`ControlifyIntegration.class` is absent. Controlify's pre-init enumerates `controlify`
entrypoints, Fabric tries to instantiate this one, and the game dies:

    Caused by: net.fabricmc.loader.api.EntrypointException: Exception while loading
      entries for entrypoint 'controlify' provided by 'zoomify'
        at dev.isxander.controlify.Controlify.preInitialiseControlify(Controlify.java:200)
    Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException:
      dev.isxander.zoomify.integrations.ControlifyIntegration

Note the top line of the crash report reads "provided by 'controlify'", so this most
likely gets misattributed to Controlify by anyone who hits it.

### Cause

`src/main/templates/fabric.mod.json` declares the `controlify` entrypoint
unconditionally, but the class it names is entirely inside a Stonecutter
`//? if controlify { … //?}` block. That constant comes from
`put("controlify", "deps.controlify".propDefined())` in `build.gradle.kts`.

`versions/26.1/gradle.properties` and `versions/26.2/gradle.properties` both define
`deps.controlify`. `versions/26.3/gradle.properties` does not — presumably because no
Controlify build for 26.3 existed when the 26.3 port (#302) landed. So the integration
is compiled out while the entrypoint declaration stays in.

Secondary effect: even without the crash, zoom-aware look sensitivity is absent on 26.3,
since that's all the integration does.

### Reproduction

Fresh Fabric 26.3 instance, nothing but:

- Fabric Loader 0.19.5
- Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3
- Fabric Language Kotlin 1.14.1+kotlin.2.4.20
- YetAnotherConfigLib 3.9.7+26.3-fabric
- Controlify 3.5.2+mc26.3
- Zoomify 2.16.2+26.3

Crashes on launch, 100% reproducible. Full crash report attached.

### Suggested fix

Either, ideally both:

1. Add `deps.controlify` to `versions/26.3/gradle.properties`. `3.5.2+mc26.3` resolves
   and builds — I've confirmed locally that the integration then compiles and the crash
   is gone.
2. Guard the `controlify` entrypoint block in `src/main/templates/fabric.mod.json` with
   the same Stonecutter condition, so a build without the dependency can't declare a
   class it doesn't ship. That prevents this recurring on the next version bump.

issues.title: Cinematic Camera slider has inverted effect, and relative sensitivity ignores the secondary zoom
issues.body:
### Version
- Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3
- Zoomify 2.16.1+26.2

## Bug 1: Cinematic Camera slider direction is inverted

The setting description says: *"How much the camera glides once moved."* — so a higher value should mean more gliding.

However `MouseMixin.modifyCinematicSmoothness` does:
```java
if (zooming && cinematicCamera > 0)
    return smoother / (cinematicCamera / 100.0);
```
- `cinematicCamera = 100` → `smoother / 1.0` → vanilla smooth-camera speed (least glide)
- `cinematicCamera = 50` → 2x smoothing
- `cinematicCamera = 10` → 10x smoothing (extreme glide)

So the lower the slider value, the stronger the smoothing — the exact opposite of the description. `cinematicCamera = 100` behaves almost like it's off.

## Bug 2: Relative sensitivity / view bobbing don't account for the secondary zoom

`previousZoomDivisor` is assigned only from the main helper:
```kotlin
zoomHelper.getZoomDivisor(tickDelta).also { previousZoomDivisor = it } * secondaryZoomHelper.getZoomDivisor(tickDelta)
```

`applyRelativeSensitivity` and `modifyBobbingIntensity` both divide by `Mth.lerp(..., previousZoomDivisor)`. During secondary-only zoom (V) the main helper is at rest (divisor = 1.0), so:
- FOV is divided by 4 (or the secondary amount), but mouse sensitivity and view bobbing are reduced by ~0 — aiming feels hypersensitive relative to the zoomed view.

### Expected
- Higher Cinematic Camera value = more glide.
- Sensitivity/bobbing scale with the effective (combined) zoom divisor.

issues.title: Secondary zoom (V) inherits scroll steps from the main zoom — extreme FOV when retainZoomSteps is on
issues.body:
### Version
- Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3
- Zoomify 2.16.1+26.2

### Summary
The secondary zoom shares the same `scrollSteps` state as the main zoom, and `getZoomDivisor()` multiplies both helpers' divisors together. When `retainZoomSteps` is enabled, the scroll position of the main zoom leaks into the secondary zoom.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Config: `"retainZoomSteps": true`, `"scrollStepCount": 10`, `"zoomPerStep": 150`, `"secondaryZoomAmount": 4`
2. Hold the zoom key (C), scroll up to max, release C (steps are retained)
3. Press the secondary zoom key (V)

### Expected
Secondary zoom gives a clean 4x zoom (its description says it is "completely separate from all other settings of Zoomify").

### Actual
The secondary zoom keeps the retained scroll position: FOV is divided by `secondaryAmount * pow(zoomPerStep/100, retainedSteps)` ≈ 4 * 1.5^10 ≈ 230x instead of 4x. Holding C and V together multiplies both: up to ~53000x zoom (essentially a black screen).

### Code reference
`Zoomify.kt`:
```kotlin
zoomHelper.tick(zooming, scrollSteps, 0)
secondaryZoomHelper.tick(secondaryZooming, scrollSteps, 0)
```
and
```kotlin
(zoomHelper.getZoomDivisor(tickDelta) * secondaryZoomHelper.getZoomDivisor(tickDelta)).toFloat()
```
The secondary helper's `tickScroll` uses the same `scrollSteps` int.

### Suggestion
Reset/ignore `scrollSteps` for the secondary helper (e.g. only pass steps when the corresponding zoom is active and the other one isn't), or clamp the combined divisor.

issues.title: Scroll zoom with zoomPerStep < 100 inverts the camera and blows up the FOV
issues.body:
### Version
- Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3
- Zoomify 2.16.1+26.2

### Config
```json
{
  "initialZoom": 4,
  "scrollZoom": true,
  "scrollStepCount": 10,
  "zoomPerStep": 60,
  "scrollZoomSmoothness": 100
}
```

### Steps to reproduce
1. Set `zoomPerStep` to a value below 100 (e.g. 60) in `zoomify.json`
2. Hold the zoom key (C) and scroll up a few steps

### Expected behaviour
Smooth zoom-in; at minimum, the mod should clamp or reject invalid values.

### Actual behaviour
The FOV explodes to thousands of degrees and the world view inverts (camera appears to spin/flip upside down). The more scroll steps, the worse it gets.

### Analysis
From the bytecode, the zoom divisor is computed roughly as:

```
divisor = (1 / initialZoomMultiplier) * pow(zoomPerStep / 100, tiers)
tiers = scrollInterpolation * scrollStepCount   // 0..10
```

With `zoomPerStep = 150` (default): `pow(1.5, 10) ≈ 57.7` — zoom in works fine.
With `zoomPerStep = 60`: `pow(0.6, 10) ≈ 0.006` — the divisor shrinks, FOV = baseFOV / divisor becomes enormous, and once the FOV exceeds 180° the view inverts.

### Suggestion
- Clamp `zoomPerStep` to a minimum of 100 (or validate it in the config screen with a warning), since values ≤ 100 make the scroll zoom either do nothing (100) or break the view entirely (<100).

issues.title: Drop Cloth Config in favour of SpruceUI
issues.body:
As of Settxi 2.9.0, I can now easily move to SpruceUI.

## Why?
Shedaniel (creator of Cloth Config) has stated that they do not recommend using Cloth anymore as the API is bad, and is only supported because they don't want to rewrite REI config.

> "cloth config is bad, don't use it" - shedaniel

## Things to consider
### OK Zoomer
As Zoomify becomes more and more advanced to fill the gap that was left on the migration to the Quilt Toolchain, the only major difference is the config screen. I don't want Zoomify to be seen as an OK Zoomer clone.

### UX
I fell the user experience in Cloth Config is marginally better than SpruceUI due to the way they handle categories. 

Cloth has a header which the user can always see and click on, making the user aware of the full capabilities immediately after opening the config.

On the SpruceUI side, the config feels busy with buttons everywhere (though they can be laid out more precisely) and categories are treated as sections, with the user having to scroll down to find the other categories. This flaw could be minimised by sorting the categories into their ascending complexity, basic users don't need to scroll, more advanced users can if they wish.

### Jar Size
Cloth Config is widely used in mods and is likely already included in modpacks or mod folders. Spruce, on the other hand, has no mod page on Curseforge nor Modrinth and relies on the mod to use Jar in Jar (though SpruceUI is more lightweight than Cloth).

## What is this issue for?
I would like to see some feedback from modpack developers and just regular users of Zoomify on what they think of the switch.

issues.body:
The zoom transition effect is highly dependent on the current framerate (like old console games).

If you have more FPS (like 120) the zoom transition is extremely smooth and fast, but if you have lower FPS (like turning on your shader) the transition can take up multiple seconds, only because the FPS is lower.

issues.title: Replicating OK Zoomer
issues.body:
I've been told that this mod aims to replicate OK Zoomer's behaviour if the user so chooses. That being said, I don't think the experience is the same yet. ### Difference 1 Attached is a [comparison video](https://eyezah.com/final/Comparison.mp4) of OK Zoomer and Zoomify (recorded at 150fps and played back at 10% speed). What's clear about this video is that that Zoomify has a more aggressive zoom IN and a less aggressive zoom OUT than OK Zoomer. OK Zoomer's logic behind this is sound: - Smooth zooming in is usually for cosmetic use (in this case, most competitive players use instant zoom), and so the mod can afford to zoom in less aggressively in order to make that shift less jarring. - Smooth zooming out, however, _needs_ to be snappy. Players stop zooming when they need to complete an activity, and so they should be able to transition out of zoom quickly, hence OK Zoomer's more aggressive zoom out. Yes, I recorded this comparison at a high framerate and the difference is small, but it's very noticeable when playing. A variation of _ease out exp_ tuned with these differences in mind would be ideal in Zoomify. ### Difference 2 OK Zoomer lets you scroll-zoom in large steps (following the same transition curve rules as above), which lets the user scroll to easily replicated levels faster. Comparatively, Zoomify scroll-zooms in smaller increments, without smooth transitions. You can see this difference in [this video](https://eyezah.com/final/ComparisonScroll.mp4) (60fps, 100% speed). Zoomify's settings were tuned to max zoom and max scroll speed in order to be comparable to OK Zoomer, by default, the scroll-zoom feels even more sluggish in Zoomify. - Zoomify gives you finer control over your zoom. - OK Zoomer lets you scroll-zoom faster. - OK Zoomer's scroll-zoom transition is less jarring that Zoomify's. To better replicate OK Zoomer, players should have the option to scroll-zoom the way OK Zoomer does.

As an OK Zoomer user trying to love Zoomify, these are the differences I've found. Besides that, the experience is identical.

issues.title: 1.18.2 crashing after launching 1.19
issues.body:
I successfully updated my game and my mods to 1.19 and played for a while. I then tried to launch 1.18.2 but the game crashes with the culprit being Zoomify. Upon investigating, it seems it is caused by zoomify.json config file. The 1.19 version is not backwards compatible with the 1.18.2 (Zoomify-1.6.0.jar) version.

It would be nice if the 1.19 config file could be updated to be compatible with its previous versions to avoid crashing. If it isn't possible, then a warning that this may happen should be added to the mod's description so people are aware of this issue.
